title: South Dakota Civics (U.S. Government) (12th Grade)
description: South Dakota Civics (U.S. Government) (12th Grade) practice - 100 questions

questions.question: A Sioux Falls class debates why a popular state statute still falls if it clashes with the United States Constitution. The governing principle is that the Constitution is:
questions.correctAnswer: The supreme law of the land, binding on every state
distractors: A model code states may adopt or ignore
Binding only on the federal government
Equal in rank to an ordinary state law
questions.explanation: Article VI declares the Constitution, federal statutes and treaties the supreme law of the land, and state judges are bound by it. A conflicting state rule cannot survive, however many voters support it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Supreme means nothing outranks it.

img.scene: A granite statehouse dome above a prairie capital city at sunrise, flag at its peak. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Supreme means nothing outranks it.
img.title: SUPREME LAW OF THE LAND

questions.question: The Constitution opens with three words that announce where governing authority originates. Those words point to:
questions.correctAnswer: The people, who grant government its power
distractors: The individual states as sovereign nations
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty is the founding premise: the people created the Constitution and remain the source of every power it delegates. Offices and branches only exercise authority the people lent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: We the People hold the power.

img.scene: Citizens of many backgrounds gathered on a town green before a white meetinghouse, morning light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: We the People hold the power.
img.title: WE THE PEOPLE

questions.question: Counting the Bill of Rights and every later change, the Constitution has been amended a known number of times. That total is:
questions.explanation: Ten amendments arrived together in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, and seventeen more followed across two centuries. The most recent, the Twenty-seventh on congressional pay, finished ratification in 1992.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ten at first, twenty-seven in all.

img.scene: A marble hall with many blank framed panels receding into soft light, none with writing. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Ten at first, twenty-seven in all.
img.title: TWENTY-SEVEN AMENDMENTS

questions.question: Two-thirds of Congress proposes an amendment. For the amendment to take effect, the Constitution next requires:
questions.correctAnswer: Ratification by three-fourths of the states
questions.explanation: Article V divides the work: Congress (or a convention) proposes, and three-fourths of the states - 38 of 50 today - ratify. The President has no formal part in the amendment process.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds propose, three-fourths ratify.

img.scene: A mosaic of many small colored stones forming a single large shield on a plaza floor, no labels. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two-thirds propose, three-fourths ratify.
img.title: HOW AMENDMENTS ARE RATIFIED

questions.question: Washington runs foreign policy while Pierre runs public schools and issues driver licenses. This division of labor is the system called:
questions.correctAnswer: Federalism - authority shared between a national government and the states
questions.explanation: Federalism assigns enumerated powers to the national government and reserves the rest to the states, with valid federal law supreme inside its sphere. Schools, policing and licensing are classic state work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two levels, each supreme in its lane.

img.scene: Two interlocking stone archways of different heights forming one gate over a country road. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two levels, each supreme in its lane.
img.title: FEDERALISM AT WORK

questions.question: A rancher asks which amendment guarantees that powers the Constitution never gave Washington stay where they started. The answer is the:
questions.explanation: The Tenth Amendment closes the Bill of Rights with the federal bargain: powers not delegated to the United States, and not forbidden to the states, are reserved to the states or to the people.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: What was never given was never lost.

img.scene: A sturdy stone wall with an open gate onto green pasture and a small town beyond. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: What was never given was never lost.
img.title: THE TENTH AMENDMENT

questions.question: Congress creates a national bank although no clause mentions banks by name. The clause that supports this is the one letting Congress pass laws that are:
questions.correctAnswer: Necessary and proper for carrying out its listed powers
distractors: Approved in advance by the state governors
questions.explanation: The Necessary and Proper Clause lets Congress choose the means to execute enumerated ends like taxing, borrowing and regulating commerce. In McCulloch v. Maryland (1819) the Court read that power broadly and shielded the bank from a state tax.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ends are listed; means are implied.

img.scene: A wide river flowing beneath a many-arched stone bridge toward a mill town. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Ends are listed; means are implied.
img.title: NECESSARY AND PROPER

questions.question: One state sues another state over Missouri River water, filing directly in the Supreme Court. The Court can take the case first because Article III grants it, for disputes between states:
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court holds original jurisdiction in cases where a state is a party, so state-versus-state suits begin and end there. Nearly everything else arrives only on appeal from a lower court.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: State against state starts at the top.

img.scene: Two riverbanks facing each other across calm water with a survey marker in the middle distance. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: State against state starts at the top.
img.title: ORIGINAL JURISDICTION

questions.question: A president who has already won two elections wonders whether an emergency permits a third run. Since 1951 the governing text is the:
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-second Amendment, capping election to the presidency at two terms
distractors: A custom dating from 1797 that binds no one
questions.explanation: George Washington's voluntary two-term example held as custom until Franklin D. Roosevelt won four elections. The Twenty-second Amendment, ratified in 1951, converted the custom into a hard legal limit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Washington set it; the 22nd locked it.

img.scene: An hourglass on a formal office desk beside a window over a capital city. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Washington set it; the 22nd locked it.
img.title: TWO-TERM LIMIT

questions.question: South Dakota tries to place its own tax on goods arriving from overseas at a river port. The attempt fails because taxing imports is among the powers the Constitution:
questions.correctAnswer: Denies to the states in Article I, Section 10
questions.explanation: Article I, Section 10 forbids states to tax imports or exports without Congress's consent, keeping one national trade policy. Taxing in general is a concurrent power, but this particular tax is fenced off.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Some powers are fenced - imports are one.

img.scene: A river port with cranes and barges at golden hour, one flag over the customs house. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Some powers are fenced - imports are one.
img.title: POWERS DENIED TO STATES

questions.question: Article I of the Constitution creates the lawmaking branch. That branch is:
questions.correctAnswer: Congress, made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Article I vests all legislative powers in a two-house Congress, a structure produced by the Great Compromise of 1787 between large-state and small-state plans.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Article I, branch one: Congress legislates.

img.scene: A grand legislative chamber with two curved banks of empty desks facing a raised rostrum. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Article I, branch one: Congress legislates.
img.title: ARTICLE I - CONGRESS

questions.question: Members of the United States House of Representatives face the voters on a cycle of:
questions.explanation: The two-year House term is the shortest in federal government, keeping the chamber drawn by population closely answerable to voters. Senators serve six years and presidents four.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: House members answer every two years.

img.scene: Two bright lanterns lit on a porch at dusk in a small prairie town, the rest dark. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: House members answer every two years.
img.title: THE TWO-YEAR HOUSE TERM

questions.question: Population decides the size of each state's delegation to the larger house of Congress, whose voting membership has been fixed since 1929 at:
questions.explanation: A 1929 statute froze the House at 435 voting seats, reapportioned among the states after each census. Adding the Senate's 100 gives 535 members of Congress in total.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 435 seats, dealt out by population.

img.scene: A vast semicircular chamber of long curved rows of empty desks stretching far back, uncountable. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: 435 seats, dealt out by population.
img.title: 435 HOUSE MEMBERS

questions.question: The Constitution sets a higher age floor for the Senate than for the House. A senator must be at least:
questions.correctAnswer: 30 years old and a citizen for nine years
distractors: 25 years old and a citizen for seven years
21 years old and a state resident for one year
questions.explanation: Senators must be 30, citizens for nine years, and residents of their state; representatives must be 25 and citizens for seven years. The framers designed the smaller chamber to be the more seasoned body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Thirty for the Senate, twenty-five for the House.

img.scene: A broad marble staircase rising to columned doors in morning sun. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Thirty for the Senate, twenty-five for the House.
img.title: WHO CAN BE A SENATOR

questions.question: The Senate splits 50-50 on a confirmation. The Constitution gives the tie-breaking vote to the:
questions.correctAnswer: Vice President, acting as President of the Senate
questions.explanation: The Vice President presides over the Senate by constitutional title and votes only when the chamber is equally divided. Ordinary days see others hold the gavel, but ties belong to the Vice President alone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The VP votes only to break a tie.

img.scene: A perfectly level balance scale on a table in a formal chamber, one chair behind it. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The VP votes only to break a tie.
img.title: BREAKING THE TIE

questions.question: The House votes to charge a federal judge with bribery, adopting formal articles against him. This charging step is called:
questions.explanation: Impeachment is accusation, not removal: a House majority adopts articles, and the Senate then conducts the trial, where two-thirds must agree to convict and remove.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The House charges; the Senate tries.

img.scene: Officials carrying a sealed document case up marble steps toward a columned building. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The House charges; the Senate tries.
img.title: THE POWER TO IMPEACH

questions.question: A tax bill must begin its journey in one specific chamber under the Origination Clause. Revenue bills start in the:
questions.explanation: Article I, Section 7 starts revenue bills in the House because its members stand closest to the taxpayers who fund them. The Senate may amend such bills once they arrive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tax bills begin closest to the taxed.

img.scene: A heavy iron key turning in the lock of a treasury vault door in warm lamplight. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Tax bills begin closest to the taxed.
img.title: WHERE TAX BILLS BEGIN

questions.question: Nine days before adjournment a bill lands on the President's desk; the President neither signs nor returns it, and Congress goes home. The bill has died by:
questions.explanation: A returned veto can be overridden by two-thirds of both houses, but a pocket veto leaves nothing to reconsider - adjournment prevented the return. It is the one presidential rejection Congress cannot answer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Unsigned and adjourned - quietly dead.

img.scene: An unopened envelope resting on an empty desk in a darkened, vacated chamber. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Unsigned and adjourned - quietly dead.
img.title: THE POCKET VETO

questions.question: A senator holds the floor for hours to stall a bill the majority supports. Ending this extended debate on most business requires a cloture vote of:
questions.explanation: Senate tradition long protected unlimited debate, so a minority could talk a measure to death. Cloture, now 60 votes for most matters, is the only brake - which makes 60 the Senate's practical working majority.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In the Senate, sixty does the work.

img.scene: A lone speaker at a podium in a large darkened chamber, one lamp glowing. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: In the Senate, sixty does the work.
img.title: THE FILIBUSTER

questions.question: After the census, a legislature draws district lines that pack opposing voters into a few districts to lock in its own advantage. The practice is known as:
questions.explanation: Redistricting itself is required so districts hold roughly equal populations; gerrymandering abuses the process so the map chooses the winners instead of the voters. The term traces to an 1812 Massachusetts district drawn like a salamander.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Maps should count voters, not pick winners.

img.scene: Oddly shaped colored fields seen from above, divided by winding streams and roads, no labels. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Maps should count voters, not pick winners.
img.title: GERRYMANDERING

questions.question: The President's branch of government exists chiefly to:
questions.correctAnswer: Execute and enforce the laws Congress enacts
questions.explanation: Article II vests executive power in the President: enforcing statutes, commanding the armed forces, conducting foreign relations and directing the departments that run federal programs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Congress writes it; the President runs it.

img.scene: A formal desk with a telephone, bound volumes and a flag in a bright office. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Congress writes it; the President runs it.
img.title: ENFORCING THE LAWS

questions.question: The heads of the executive departments, gathered to advise the President as one body, form the:
questions.explanation: From Washington's four advisers the Cabinet has grown to fifteen department heads, each nominated by the President, confirmed by the Senate and serving at the President's pleasure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fifteen departments, one advisory table.

img.scene: A long polished table with high-backed chairs in a formal meeting room, flags at the far end. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Fifteen departments, one advisory table.
img.title: THE CABINET

questions.question: If the presidency and vice presidency fall vacant together, the 1947 succession statute turns first to an elected official - the:
distractors: President pro tempore of the Senate
questions.explanation: The Presidential Succession Act of 1947 places the Speaker second in line, then the president pro tempore, then Cabinet secretaries starting with State - deliberately favoring elected over appointed officials.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Speaker stands second in line.

img.scene: A row of empty high-backed chairs arranged in order along a paneled wall. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Speaker stands second in line.
img.title: LINE OF SUCCESSION

questions.question: Without any new statute, a president orders agencies to change how an existing law is administered. The instrument used is an:
questions.explanation: Executive orders direct the executive branch with the force of law, but they rest below statutes: Congress can override them by legislation, courts can strike them down, and a successor can revoke them by signature.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: An order directs agencies - Congress can answer.

img.scene: A fountain pen resting on a document folder on a desk, seal blurred and unreadable. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: An order directs agencies - Congress can answer.
img.title: EXECUTIVE ORDERS

questions.question: A treaty negotiated by the President takes effect only after consent from:
questions.explanation: Article II shares the treaty power: the President negotiates, but two-thirds of senators present must consent. That high bar is one reason presidents often use executive agreements instead.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Treaties need two-thirds of the Senate.

img.scene: Two delegations shaking hands across a long table by tall windows over a river. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Treaties need two-thirds of the Senate.
img.title: THE TREATY POWER

questions.question: A federal judge issues an unpopular ruling, yet she cannot be voted out or fired for it, because Article III judges hold office:
questions.correctAnswer: During good behavior - in practice for life
questions.explanation: Life tenure insulates judges from retaliation for lawful but unpopular decisions; pay cannot be cut for the same reason. Federal judges leave by retirement, death, or impeachment and removal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Life tenure shields hard rulings.

img.scene: An empty judge's bench in a quiet wood-paneled courtroom in a shaft of daylight. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Life tenure shields hard rulings.
img.title: LIFE TENURE FOR JUDGES

questions.question: The Supreme Court first claimed the power to strike down an act of Congress in the 1803 decision:
questions.explanation: Chief Justice Marshall's opinion in Marbury reasoned that judges sworn to uphold the Constitution cannot enforce a statute that violates it. Judicial review is inferred from the document, never spelled out in it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Marbury made courts the referees.

img.scene: A marble courthouse facade with tall columns and broad steps at midday. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Marbury made courts the referees.
img.title: MARBURY V. MADISON

questions.question: An indigent defendant faces a felony charge and cannot hire counsel. Under Gideon v. Wainwright (1963), the state must:
questions.correctAnswer: Appoint a lawyer for him at public expense
distractors: Fine him for the cost of the trial
questions.explanation: Clarence Gideon's handwritten petition produced a unanimous ruling: counsel is a fundamental right, so states must provide an attorney to felony defendants who cannot afford one. The guarantee later reached cases risking jail time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No money for counsel? The state provides one.

img.scene: A single sheet of paper and a pencil on a plain table in a small quiet room. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: No money for counsel? The state provides one.
img.title: GIDEON'S RIGHT TO COUNSEL

questions.question: Officers interrogate a man in custody without advising him of his rights, and his statement is excluded at trial. The exclusion follows the warnings required by:
questions.explanation: Miranda held custodial questioning inherently pressuring, so statements taken without warnings - the rights to silence and to an attorney, appointed if necessary - cannot be used by prosecutors.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Silent and counseled - Miranda's shields.

img.scene: A quiet interrogation room with a table, two chairs and a bright window, no people near the camera. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Silent and counseled - Miranda's shields.
img.title: MIRANDA WARNINGS

questions.question: In Brown v. Board of Education (1954) the Court held that racially separate public schools are, by their nature:
questions.correctAnswer: Inherently unequal under the Fourteenth Amendment
distractors: A question each state settles for itself
questions.explanation: Brown discarded Plessy's separate-but-equal doctrine in education, finding that separation itself stamps children with a sense of inferiority. The ruling became the legal foundation of the modern civil-rights era.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Separate schools are unequal schools.

img.scene: Children of different backgrounds climbing the steps of a brick schoolhouse together in morning sun. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Separate schools are unequal schools.
img.title: BROWN V. BOARD

questions.question: Ratified together in 1791, the first ten amendments are collectively called the:
questions.explanation: The Bill of Rights answered Anti-Federalist fears of a strong national government by naming the freedoms it may not touch - speech, religion, due process and more - against federal power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ten amendments calmed the ratification fight.

img.scene: Ten tall blank parchment panels hanging in a row in a museum hall under soft spotlights. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Ten amendments calmed the ratification fight.
img.title: THE BILL OF RIGHTS

questions.question: A Rapid City newspaper investigates city contracts and officials move to silence it. The amendment a court invokes for the paper is the:
questions.explanation: Freedom of the press sits in the First Amendment, and the Fourteenth Amendment carries that limit onto state and local governments. Criticism of officials is the core case press freedom exists to protect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Criticizing officials is protected speech.

img.scene: A vintage printing press in a workshop with stacks of blank paper in warm light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Criticizing officials is protected speech.
img.title: FREEDOM OF THE PRESS

questions.question: A city permits every group except one faith to gather in its park. The ban collides with the First Amendment protections of:
questions.correctAnswer: Free exercise of religion and assembly
questions.explanation: The First Amendment packs five freedoms together - religion, speech, press, assembly and petition. Singling out one faith's worship burdens free exercise, and barring its gathering burdens assembly at the same time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Five freedoms share the First Amendment.

img.scene: People of many faiths walking through a public park with a bandstand in autumn light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Five freedoms share the First Amendment.
img.title: FREE EXERCISE AND ASSEMBLY

questions.question: Before officers may search a home for evidence, the Fourth Amendment generally requires a warrant supported by:
questions.correctAnswer: Probable cause, particularly describing the place and the items sought
distractors: A majority vote of the neighbors
questions.explanation: The Fourth Amendment bans unreasonable searches and demands specific warrants - no open-ended rummaging. Courts allow narrow exceptions, but probable cause plus particularity is the default rule.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No warrant, no rummage.

img.scene: A farmhouse front door with a brass knocker and a garden path in peaceful morning light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: No warrant, no rummage.
img.title: THE FOURTH AMENDMENT

questions.question: A witness refuses to answer a prosecutor's question because the answer would incriminate her. The protection she invokes lives in the:
questions.explanation: The Fifth Amendment bundles several shields: grand jury indictment, no double jeopardy, no compelled self-incrimination, due process, and just compensation when property is taken for public use.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Fifth lets you stay silent.

img.scene: A witness stand with a microphone and a glass of water in an empty courtroom. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Fifth lets you stay silent.
img.title: THE RIGHT TO SILENCE

questions.question: Bail is set at ten million dollars on a minor theft charge. The Eighth Amendment objection is that the bail is:
questions.correctAnswer: Excessive - bail exists to secure appearance, not to punish
questions.explanation: Bail calibrated far beyond what ensures a defendant's return stops being security and becomes punishment before trial, which the Eighth Amendment forbids alongside cruel and unusual punishments.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bail ensures return - it is not punishment.

img.scene: Balance scales tipped absurdly by one enormous weight against a tiny coin, symbolic still life. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Bail ensures return - it is not punishment.
img.title: EXCESSIVE BAIL

questions.question: The Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments were adopted in the years right after the Civil War and are grouped as the:
questions.explanation: The trio rebuilt American citizenship in sequence: the Thirteenth abolished slavery in 1865, the Fourteenth defined citizenship with equal protection in 1868, and the Fifteenth barred racial denial of the vote in 1870.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 13 freed, 14 defined, 15 voted.

img.scene: A stone bridge rebuilt after a storm, three strong new arches over a river. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: 13 freed, 14 defined, 15 voted.
img.title: RECONSTRUCTION AMENDMENTS

questions.question: A woman voting for the first time in the 1920 election relies on the amendment ratified that year - the:
questions.explanation: Ratified in 1920 after a campaign stretching back to Seneca Falls in 1848, the Nineteenth Amendment forbade denying the vote on account of sex and roughly doubled the eligible electorate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1920: sex could no longer bar the ballot.

img.scene: Women in period dress marching peacefully down a main street with blank banners, period photograph style. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: 1920: sex could no longer bar the ballot.
img.title: THE NINETEENTH AMENDMENT

questions.question: A state demands a payment before a citizen may vote in a federal contest. The Twenty-fourth Amendment makes the practice:
questions.correctAnswer: Unconstitutional - poll taxes are forbidden in federal elections
distractors: Lawful if the amount is small
A free choice for each state
questions.explanation: Poll taxes priced poor voters - disproportionately Black Southerners - out of federal elections until the Twenty-fourth Amendment banned them in 1964; the courts soon extended the ban to state elections as well.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Voting is a right, not a purchase.

img.scene: An empty ballot box beside a price tag torn in half on a table, symbolic. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Voting is a right, not a purchase.
img.title: NO POLL TAX

questions.question: Drafted eighteen-year-olds in 1971 won the vote through the fastest-ratified amendment in American history, the:
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-sixth Amendment, fixing the voting age at 18
questions.explanation: 'Old enough to fight, old enough to vote' moved the Twenty-sixth Amendment through the states in about one hundred days in 1971. The Twenty-third grants DC electors; the Twenty-fifth covers presidential disability.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fight at 18 meant vote at 18.

img.scene: Young voters at a row of voting booths in a school gymnasium, seen from behind. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Fight at 18 meant vote at 18.
img.title: VOTING AT EIGHTEEN

questions.question: Two engineers on temporary work visas in Rapid City welcome a daughter delivered at the local hospital. Because of where she was born, the Fourteenth Amendment makes the newborn:
questions.correctAnswer: A citizen of the United States by birth
distractors: A citizen only if Congress votes to admit her
A citizen of the parents' country only
questions.explanation: The Fourteenth Amendment's first sentence grants citizenship to all persons born or naturalized in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction. The Supreme Court applied it to children of non-citizen residents in United States v. Wong Kim Ark (1898).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Born here means citizen here.

img.scene: A newborn's bassinet beside a window in soft daylight, a small flag on the sill. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Born here means citizen here.
img.title: BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP

questions.question: A lawful permanent resident completes residence, testing and an oath to become a citizen. That legal process is called:
questions.explanation: Naturalization is the statutory path Congress sets for immigrants: a residence period, English and civics testing, good moral character, and finally the oath of allegiance in a public ceremony.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Naturalization turns residents into citizens.

img.scene: A raised hand taking an oath in a bright courtroom ceremony, flags at the front, seen from behind. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Naturalization turns residents into citizens.
img.title: NATURALIZATION

questions.question: Registering with Selective Service on turning 18, paying taxes and serving when called to a jury are best classified as a citizen's:
distractors: Privileges the government may withdraw at will
Rights guaranteed by the First Amendment
questions.explanation: Duties are mandatory and enforced by law. Responsibilities - voting, staying informed, volunteering - are voluntary, yet self-government depends on citizens actually doing them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Duties are compelled; responsibilities are chosen.

img.scene: A mailbox and community notice boards in a town square in morning light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Duties are compelled; responsibilities are chosen.
img.title: DUTIES VS RESPONSIBILITIES

questions.question: Presidential elections turn on the Electoral College, where 538 electors are pledged. The number needed to win the White House is:
distractors: A plurality of the national popular vote
questions.explanation: Each state's electors equal its House seats plus two senators, with three more for the District of Columbia - 538 in all, so a majority is 270. Failing that, the House decides by state delegation.

questions.question: Federal elections held in South Dakota - for President, Senate and House - are administered day to day at the local level chiefly by:
questions.correctAnswer: County auditors, under South Dakota election law
distractors: The Federal Election Commission's field offices
questions.explanation: Standard 9-12.C.16.B teaches the federal election process 'based on South Dakota law': the secretary of state oversees the system statewide, while elected county auditors run registration, ballots and polling in their counties.

questions.question: South Dakota women won full voting rights through a state constitutional amendment in a year that places the state ahead of the national change. That year was:
distractors: 1920 - the same year as the Nineteenth Amendment
questions.explanation: After decades of campaigns (and partial school-election suffrage earlier), South Dakota voters approved full women's suffrage in November 1918, two years before the Nineteenth Amendment nationalized it. Suffrage history is part of the state's grade 8 and civics story.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1918: South Dakota moved first.

questions.question: South Dakota's chief election officer - the statewide official who oversees voter registration systems and certifies election results - is the:
distractors: Commissioner of School and Public Lands
questions.explanation: The secretary of state, one of the independently elected constitutional officers, supervises elections statewide under South Dakota law, while county auditors conduct them locally - the two-level structure in 9-12.C.16.B and C.17.D.

questions.question: Standard 9-12.C.17.E requires students to study the tribal governments within South Dakota. The number of federally recognized tribes with governments in the state is:
questions.explanation: South Dakota is home to nine federally recognized tribal governments, among them the Oglala Sioux Tribe, Rosebud Sioux Tribe, Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe and Standing Rock Sioux Tribe. Each is a sovereign government, not a private association.

questions.question: The tribal government based at Pine Ridge, the largest reservation in South Dakota by population, is the:
questions.explanation: The Oglala Sioux Tribe governs the Pine Ridge Reservation in southwestern South Dakota, operating under its own constitution and an elected tribal council led by a tribal president.

questions.correctAnswer: Oceti Sakowin - the Seven Council Fires
questions.explanation: Oceti Sakowin names the historic alliance of seven council fires - the Lakota, Dakota and Nakota peoples. The Oceti Sakowin Essential Understandings carry this history into South Dakota classrooms alongside the state standards.

questions.question: A tribal government in South Dakota adopts laws, runs courts and police, and enrolls its own citizens. In law, this authority rests on the tribe's status as a:
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereign government whose powers predate the United States
questions.explanation: Tribal sovereignty is inherent: tribes governed themselves long before 1776, and treaties and federal law recognize them as distinct political communities. Standard 9-12.C.17.E-F builds the state course on exactly this point.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sovereign before the Union existed.

questions.question: Many South Dakota tribal governments operate under written constitutions and elected councils organized in the era of the:
questions.explanation: The Indian Reorganization Act ended the allotment policy and supported tribal self-government; several South Dakota tribes adopted constitutions under it providing for elected councils, presidents and tribal courts. Some tribes, like the Oglala, later amended theirs substantially.

questions.question: The federal government's legal duties toward the tribes - protecting tribal lands and resources held in trust - grow chiefly out of the historic instruments called:
questions.correctAnswer: Treaties between the United States and the tribes
questions.explanation: Treaties such as the Fort Laramie Treaties of 1851 and 1868 were agreements between sovereigns, and they ground the federal trust responsibility. The Supreme Court treats treaties as the supreme law of the land alongside the Constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Treaties created the trust duty.

questions.question: The Treaty of Fort Laramie (1868) is central to South Dakota civics because it:
questions.correctAnswer: Established the Great Sioux Reservation, covering western South Dakota including the Black Hills
distractors: Opened the Black Hills to gold miners
Created the state of South Dakota
Ended all tribal governments in Dakota Territory
questions.explanation: The 1868 treaty set aside the Great Sioux Reservation for the Sioux and required tribal consent for any land cession. The later seizure of the Black Hills after gold was found there remains a live legal and moral dispute - the Sioux have refused a monetary award, holding out for the land itself.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1868 promised the Hills; the fight continues.

questions.question: A crime is committed by a tribal citizen on reservation land in South Dakota. As an outline, criminal jurisdiction in Indian country depends on:
questions.correctAnswer: Who the people involved are and where it happened - tribal, federal and state authority divide by those facts
distractors: State law alone, exactly as anywhere else in South Dakota
No government's law - reservations are law-free zones
questions.explanation: Indian country jurisdiction is famously layered: tribes hold authority over their own citizens, federal law covers major crimes and interracial cases, and state authority generally stops at reservation borders for tribal citizens. Standard 9-12.C.17.F asks for this outline, not courtroom detail.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Who and where decide who judges.

questions.question: South Dakota's county governments - the layer between the state and its cities and townships - number:

questions.question: Standard 9-12.C.17.C sends students to study the structure of their own local government. In a typical South Dakota city, that structure is headed by:
questions.correctAnswer: An elected mayor and city council (in some cities, a commission or a council with an appointed city manager)
questions.explanation: South Dakota municipalities choose among mayor-council, commission and council-manager forms, but the constant is elected local leadership accountable to city voters - with townships and counties completing the local layers C.17.C names.
